forbidden_semantic_inputs: commit messages/diffs/file snippets or unrelated metadata exposed only while resolving repository head
policy.feedback_use: mechanical self-local QC only; never infer novelty/relevance/acceptance/ranking/preferred mechanism
policy.own_state_resolution: LATEST/STATE first; otherwise newest source-qualified role-local checkpoint by repository chronology; minimum predecessor chain; quarantine accidental stale/cross-role observability reads
policy.scope_guard: never broaden evidence beyond tested scope
policy.continuation: open-ended; checkpoints/findings are never global completion; maintain nonempty frontier and exact next action until hard runtime/tool termination
policy.receipt_rule: write immutable own receipt only; never read aggregate ledger or other receipts
policy.control_freshness: obtain note main SHA only via Git ref-object lookup such as refs/heads/main or equivalent SHA-only response; never use generic commit/search/branch payloads for head freshness. Read sanitized DESIRED_STATE and this role config at that SHA; repeat SHA-only ref lookup before the first role-local/public-source semantic read and refetch if control/config changed; quarantine/discard excess connector semantic payload.
policy.semantic_freeze_barrier: The first role-local state, feedback, or public-source semantic read freezes exactly one semantic control tuple {note_main_sha, control_revision, config_revision, role_config_blob} for the entire physical invocation. Never adopt a second control/config revision after this barrier. If a newer control is detected before the barrier, refetch it and restart the pre-semantic bootstrap before proceeding. If a newer control is detected after the barrier, stop new semantic work, checkpoint results under the already-frozen tuple, record control_change_after_semantic_start=true plus the newer observed revision only as non-semantic continuation metadata, and adopt it on the next scheduled invocation. A receipt must report exactly one semantic control/config tuple; do not reinterpret or extend outputs under a newer config in the same invocation.
